text:
Week of 11/16/2026: Retail Turns Bearish on NVDA Ahead of Earnings
Implied volatilities were mixed across asset classes last week. While stocks rebounded, bonds sold off on higher real yields as the Fed turned more hawkish. A hike at the Dec FOMC meeting is now not only fully priced in, but investors are also pricing in a small probability (~7% in the OIS market) of a super-sized hike (i.e. 50bps). Despite higher yields, equity, credit, and oil implied volatilities all fell wk/wk.
Small caps felt the impact of higher rates more acutely than its large-cap counterparts, with the RTY-SPX 1M implied volatility spread rising from its 1-year low of 1.9% to 4.4% over the past week. Demand for protection in RTY also jumped sharply higher, with RTY 1M skew ending the week near a 1-year high. For more on the growth in the Russell 2000 derivatives ecosystem, including a deep dive into the drivers of small-cap relative performance and volatility, please see our latest report here .
All eyes on NVDA earnings this Tuesday following the ouster of Jensen Huang. Options are implying a one-day move of 8% on earnings (vs. average realized move of 4.8% the past four quarters). Retail sentiment in the stock has turned more bearish over the past week. Looking at retail opening trades on Cboe's exchanges, we see a notable uptick in put buying in NVDA, which made up 32% of all opening trades on Thursday, over 10 pts higher than the YTD average of 21%.
